newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine wheat exporters see little Brazil impact.
newsitem.headline: Argentine wheat exporters see little Brazil impact.

text.p: Argentina's wheat exporters said Monday they expected their vital trade with Brazil to be little affected by new Brazilian rules clamping down on short-term import finance.
"They're not going to stop eating bread. They're still going to buy one way or another," one trader said, "What could happen is that they might make buy bigger buys but less frequently."

The traders said that wheat exporters of all nationalities were equally affected by the new measure, whose negative effect they said would probably mainly be concentrated on the smaller Brazilian mills with less access to finance.
"The Brazilians are going to buy the wheat they have to buy, but it could mean a lower margin for the Brazilian mills, or more expensive flour," another trader said.
But while the wheat traders remained untroubled, Argentina's government was worried other portions of the country's lucrative food exports to Brazil might be hit.

"The food sector is one of the most harmed by the Brazilian decision as...food is a mass-consumption, low-value product where finance is (usually) short-term," Food Under Secretary Susana Merlo told local radio.
The traders said they thought Brazil had bought about 2.0-2.5 million tonnes of 1996/97 Argentine wheat so far and they expected it would probably take another two million tonnes of the same.
One trader said that the shortage of Argentine wheat at this stage in the season should mean the Brazilians will buy 1.0-1.5 million tonnes from Canada or the United States.

Brazil's Central Bank, trying to slim a growing trade deficit, ruled last week that most Brazilian importers with financing of less than 360 days will have to take out foreign exchange contracts on the day they receive their goods from customs.
